summary.name: WhisPaste
summary.one_liner: WhisPaste is a push-to-talk desktop dictation app that transcribes speech on-device with Whisper or Parakeet and pastes the text at the cursor in any app.
use_cases: Writing text by voice in any text field
Hands-free text entry with a hotkey
Sending chat messages by voice without touching the keyboard
summary.what_it_does: WhisPaste records speech while you hold a hotkey or tap it to start and stop, then transcribes it and pastes the text into the active text field. Transcription runs on-device using Whisper or Parakeet models. It can automatically raise quiet speech before recognition, with an adjustable input volume. Profiles let you set language, speech model, Smart Mode, microphone and output per app, and each profile can have its own hotkey. Users can favorite up to five recognition languages and switch between them with a shortcut.
notable: Per-app profiles with their own language, model, microphone and optional hotkey
Automatic quiet-speech leveling that does not amplify silence or clip loud passages
Optional 'Send after pasting' presses Enter after dictation, and music/video pause while dictating on Windows and Linux
caveats: Holding the hotkey to record is experimental on Linux
'Send after pasting' works on Linux only with X11
Recordings stop automatically after 2 minutes by default (adjustable)
